original_question: How can one microscopically derive the full five-dimensional Bohr-Mottelson quadrupole collective Hamiltonian by extending a one-dimensional collective path to a two-dimensional collective hypersurface that can be mapped onto the beta-gamma plane, while also evaluating rotational moments of inertia at non-equilibrium points in a fully self-consistent way?
target_in_paper: The procedure in Sec. 5.1 for the microscopic derivation of the Bohr–Mottelson collective Hamiltonian, wherein the moving-frame HFB states |ϕ(q)〉 defining a two-dimensional collective submanifold (q₁,q₂) in the TDHFB phase space are mapped one-to-one onto the (β,γ) deformation plane as a collective hypersurface via Eqs. (42)–(43) and Fig. 3, and the rotational moments of inertia J_k(β,γ) are obtained at every point on this (β,γ) plane by solving the Thouless–Valatin (LQRPA) equations (Eq. 52) off the equilibrium.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies: the goal of microscopically deriving the full five-dimensional Bohr–Mottelson quadrupole collective Hamiltonian; the need to extend from a one-dimensional collective path to a two-dimensional collective hypersurface mapped onto the β–γ plane; and the self-consistent evaluation of rotational moments of inertia at non-equilibrium deformations.
missing_details: Definition of the moving-frame HFB state |ϕ(q)〉 obtained from the moving-frame HFB equation (Eq. 40)
Specification that collective coordinates (q₁,q₂) are canonical variables corresponding to β and γ via the expectation values in Eqs. (42)–(43)
Use of the local QRPA (LQRPA) equations (Eqs. 44–45) to extract vibrational inertial masses B_i(q) on the hypersurface
Assumption that the mapping between (q₁,q₂) and (β,γ) is one-to-one in the neighborhood of each point
Quantization of the resulting curvilinear Hamiltonian by the Pauli prescription (Appendix A) to obtain the final collective Schrödinger equation
Recognition that the generators for rotational motion are the angular-momentum operators Î_k and their conjugate angle operators Ψ̂_k(q) (Eqs. 50–51)
Explicit mention that rotational inertia J_k(q) is the inverse of B_k(q) and computed via the Thouless–Valatin equations (Eq. 52) at off-equilibrium points
Structure of the full collective Hamiltonian H_coll = T_vib(β,γ)+T_rot(β,γ)+V(β,γ)
Reference to the curvilinear form of the kinetic energy terms and the scale transformation making B_i(q)=1 for vibrational masses
refined_question: How can one, within the moving-frame HFB plus local QRPA framework described in Sec. 5.1, derive the full five-dimensional Bohr–Mottelson quadrupole collective Hamiltonian by: (i) solving the moving-frame HFB equation (Eq. 40) at each point (q₁,q₂) of the two-dimensional collective submanifold to obtain |ϕ(q)〉; (ii) defining the β and γ deformation variables via Eqs. (42)–(43) and mapping (q₁,q₂) one-to-one onto the (β,γ) plane as a collective hypersurface (Fig. 3); (iii) computing the vibrational inertial masses B_i(β,γ) through the LQRPA equations (Eqs. 44–45); (iv) determining the three rotational moments of inertia J_k(β,γ) by solving the Thouless–Valatin equations (Eq. 52) at every off-equilibrium (β,γ) point; and (v) quantizing the resulting curvilinear kinetic energy terms by the Pauli prescription to obtain the quantized 5D collective Schrödinger equation?
justification: The draft question directly refers to the mapping of the two-dimensional collective coordinates onto the β–γ plane as a collective hypersurface and the evaluation of rotational moments of inertia at non-equilibrium deformations, which are precisely formulated in Sec. 5.1 of the paper (Eqs. 42–43, Fig. 3) and in the subsequent discussion of rotational inertia (Eq. 52). However, it omits several critical procedural and definitional details—such as the moving-frame HFB equation (40), the LQRPA equations (44–45), the Pauli quantization, and the definitions of the infinitesimal generators—that are necessary to render the question self-contained and faithful to the paper’s intent.
